targeted.documentation: Both examples executed independently; raw result matches dense to 1e-12.

pytest.workflow: check_all.sh passed black, mypy and all three pylint checks, but its pytest phase stalled in an existing nested TensorFlow interface test with TF_NUM_INTEROP_THREADS=1. After all other workers completed, that run was interrupted. The entire interface module passed with TF_NUM_INTEROP_THREADS=4. Results were matched by node ID against a fresh complete collection; no cases were omitted. Both Sphinx builds then passed separately.

model.hamiltonian: 0.7 sum Z_i Z_(i+1) + 0.3 sum Z_i + (0.6 cos(0.9 t) + 0.2) sum X_i
model.collapse: sqrt(0.08) (X_i + i Y_i)/2 and sqrt(0.03) Z_i

error_metrics.max_entry: max over output times and matrix entries of abs(rho - reference)
error_metrics.relative_frobenius: max over output times of norm(rho - reference, Frobenius) / norm(reference, Frobenius)
error_metrics.trace: max over output times of abs(trace(rho) - 1)
error_metrics.hermiticity: max over output times and matrix entries of abs(rho - rho.adjoint())

methodology: Shared Xeon Platinum 8458P CPU. All forward timings and the 8-qubit work-precision curves use one pinned logical CPU and one BLAS thread per comparison cohort, with four warmed samples per method in two mirrored cycles. Only within-cohort ratios are compared. QuTiP MESolver is built once per worker; TC is compiled once per worker. Returned density matrices are materialized for both methods. No output normalization. The separate 10-qubit tight-accuracy check uses the same eight pinned logical CPUs and eight BLAS threads for both methods; its runtime is excluded from the performance comparisons. The 9-qubit tight-accuracy check uses one CPU/thread. A single-CPU attempt at the 10-qubit accuracy check was stopped before its first result and restarted on eight CPUs; none of the completed timed samples were changed.
